sentences.text: Deepu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 February, 2023

Author: Siddharth
Bench: Siddharth
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
 Reserved On:- 15.02.2023 
 Delivered On:- 21.02.2023 
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 25328 of 2022 
Applicant :- Deepu 
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others 
Counsel for Applicant :- Vishvendra Singh 
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kamal Singh,Sandeep Mishra
Hon'ble Siddharth, J.
1. Heard Sri Vishvendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Pawan Kumar Shukla,
Advocate, holding brief of Sri Harish Chandra, learned counsel for the informant and learned Aga
of the State.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. There is allegation against the applicant of abduction of minor girl with intent to marry,
commission of offence of rape, illegal confinement, conspiracy and penetrative sexual assault in the
Fir.
3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submits that it is a case of false implication.
In the FIR, there is allegation that the applicant enticed away the minor daughter of informant at 11:00 pm in the night.
Co-accused, Rakhi, assisted the applicant in the alleged offence.
The offence took place on 28.02.2022.
The medico-legal examination of the victim was conducted on 03.03.2022 wherein no sign of rape was found but victim was found to be minor aged about 15 years.
Supplementary medical report of the victim also does not implicates the applicant.

He has further submitted that the prosecution allegations in the FIR have later been partly denied by her mother and also the victim by stating that the co-accused, Rakhi, was falsely implicated by them because of dispute with Deepu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172157814/
1 the informant and she has no role in the incident.

entities.text: Deepu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before the doctor the victim has made allegation against co-accused, Rakhi, and has also stated that the applicant married her by putting vermilion in her hair.
Thereafter the elder brother of the applicant called her parents and she was sent to her home.
4. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 07.03.2022.
The victim eloped with the applicant and thereafter elder brother of the applicant called her parents and she went back with them.
It is a case of false implication.
The applicant in jail since 17.03.2022 and has no criminal history to his credit.

5. Counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A have vehemently opposed the bail application of the applicant and has submitted that since the victim is minor and has made allegation against the applicant, it is not a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
6.
After hearing the rival contentions, this Court finds that although the victim is minor as per her ossification test report but the prosecution case is not much reliable.
The medical report also does not supports the prosecution case.
Hence, the applicant is deserves to be enlarged on bail.

7. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused; submissions of the learned counsel for the parties noted above; finding force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant; keeping view the uncertainty regarding conclusion of trial; one sided investigation by police, ignoring the case of accused side; applicants being under-trial having fundamental right to speedy trial; larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India;
considering the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I., passed in S.L.P (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021; considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by the under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicants have made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant, Deepu, involved in Case Crime No. 120 of 2022, under Sections- 363, 366, 376,
342, 120-B IPC and Section  of POCSO Act, Police Station- Tajganj, District- Agra, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or as directed by the Court.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Deepu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172157814/
2 Penal Code.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case, of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
